sentences.text: Shri Ashish Gupta, learned counsel for the appellant  Shri Bharat Yadav, learned counsel for the responden  on behalf of Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta, Advocate.

ORDER The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 8.2.2024 passed in Claim Case No.115/2022, whereby challenging quantum of compensation.
The liability of Insurance Company due to the death in the accident by insured vehicle is not under dispute.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 7.11.2021 deceased Durga was going as pillion rider alongwith her husband.

When they reached just ahead of Manavar-Kukshi Toll Tax Barrier near village Dedla,
the rider of motorcycle No.MP-11-MB-9199 came riding the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed into motorcycle of deceased from behind, because of which deceased Durga fell down from the motorcycle and sustained injuries on her head, because of which blood started oozing from her ear.
She was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29003 2 MA-7705-2024 rushed to Manavar Hospital through 108 Ambulance, from where she was referred to Barwani.
When her condition did not improve she was shifted to Aurobindo Hospital, Indore.
Thereafter, she was referred to Gujrat at Dheeraj Hospital, where she died during treatment.
2.1 The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Durga.

The claims Tribunal after considering the evidence available on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,65,100/-, out of which an amount of Rs.5,37,600/-
was for loss of dependency.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that before the claims Tribunal it was claimed and established that deceased was earning Rs.9,000/- per month by doing the Labour work.
In support of this claim appellant No.1 examined himself as PW-1.

However, the claims Tribunal disbelieved Pappu Thakur vs Dinesh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130587664/
1 the same and only Rs.3,000/- per month was taken as her income on notional basis.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that the consequential compensation because of incorrect assessment of income is very less.

He further submits that even if the income has to be assessed on notional basis, then also at least minimum wages should have been fixed because of contribution of house wife has been considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court not lesser than of an earning member of the family.

As such,
in any case, income should not have been assessed on notional basis, but the same should have been assessed on minimum wages prescribed for the unskilled Labour.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance company submits that in para 16 of the cross-examination appellant No.1 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29003 3 MA-7705-2024 himself had admitted that he has not produced any document with respect to income of the deceased.
Hence, the claims Tribunal has correctly assessed the income on notional basis at Rs.3,000/- per month.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.
6.
Apart from the question of income of the deceased no other ground has been raised by either of the parties.

From the findings of the claims Tribunal in para 24 and 25 of the impugned award it is seen that the claims Tribunal has considered the statement of appellant No.1 (PW-1) and after noting that the appellant No.1 himself admitted in para 16 of the cross- examination that he has not produced any material to establish income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month assessed her income on notional basis at Rs.3,000/- per month.

However, as has been repeatedly held by the Hon'ble Apex Court starting from the case of Lata Wadhwa Vs. State of Bhiar , reported in AIR 2001 SC 3218 to the latest one in the case of Kirti Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., reported in (2021) 2 SCC 166 , the contribution of house maker, if the deceased is not considered as working member of the family can also not be taken any lesser than earning member of the family.

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa Vs. State of Bhiar , reported in AIR 2001 SC 3218
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kirti Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., reported in (2021) 2 SCC 166
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, this Court is of the considered view that at least minimum wages prescribed at the relevant time i.e. on 7.11.2021 for an unskilled Labour has to be taken into account.
As per guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority the minimum wages were Rs.8,500/- per month.
As such, the same is taken as income of the deceased.

Consequently, after applying all the parameters by the claims Tribunal, the compensation for loss of dependency NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29003 4 MA-7705-2024 would change to Rs.15,23,200/- and after deducting the already awarded amount of Rs.7,65,100/-, the appellants are now entitled for payment of compensation of Rs.9,85,600/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim application till its payment.
7. It is seen from the record that appeal has been valued at Rs.7,00,000/-, the appellants are directed to pay deficit Court fees within a period of four weeks from today.
In case of failure to pay deficit Court fees within the period of four weeks, the appellants will not be entitled for interest beyond the period of four weeks.
8. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Pappu Thakur vs Dinesh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130587664/
